items.title: The Pearl of Great Price: Unearthing the 19th-Century Composite Mormon 'Scripture'
items.summary: A Mormon News Roundup YouTube video examines the Pearl of Great Price, a book of Latter-day Saint scripture, and argues it is a composite of 19th-century material.

items.title: We now know when the Salt Lake LDS Temple will truly be a ‘temple’ again
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that the First Presidency announced the renovated Salt Lake Temple will be rededicated Dec. 5, 2027, with members holding temple recommends able to attend ceremonies the following Monday. The Tribune says the gap after the open house ends is meant to give crews time to clean and repair the building.

items.title: How the LDS Church Endangers Children—and What Must Change
items.summary: An Exponent II blog post by a contributor says Wade Christofferson, brother of President D. Todd Christofferson, was sentenced to 45 years in federal prison on Nov. 17, and asks who authorized removing a warning from his membership record. The post also criticizes a youth activity in a church magazine and calls for stronger child-protection practices.

items.title: (Not So) Hot Take: Let’s Stop Defending Institutional Racism
items.summary: A By Common Consent post by MDH argues that common faithful responses to the temple and priesthood ban from 1852 to 1978 defend the policy, and says the church’s own essays show it was rooted in racism. The author asks why church leadership does not say so plainly.

items.title: Former Mormon Church Abuse Hotline Lawyer!
items.summary: On Radio Free Mormon, Meggan Hayes and Kolby Reddish discuss an interview with Kate Lauck, a former Kirton-McConkie lawyer who worked on the church’s abuse hotline, and question her account of the hotline and her grasp of the law.

items.title: Utah’s Deidre Henderson has come a long way since losing her first election and hiding in the bathroom
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune publishes excerpts from its “Mormon Land” podcast with Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson, a Latter-day Saint who refused a Justice Department demand for the state’s unredacted voter rolls. She says her faith helped her act on conviction regardless of the consequences.

items.title: Salt Lake Temple will be dedicated for the third time at the end of 2027
items.summary: Deseret News reports that the First Presidency announced the renovated Salt Lake Temple will be rededicated on Sunday, Dec. 5, 2027, following the public open house that runs April 5 through Oct. 1, 2027.

items.title: Did Latter-day Saints in Utah shift left? What the latest polls tell us
items.summary: Deseret News reports that polling indicates most Utah Latter-day Saints still identify as Republicans, though Republican identification fell from 83% to 75%, which the article largely attributes to lower turnout rather than a change in party identity.

items.title: Dr. Gregory Prince: The Mormon Faith Crisis and the Church’s Crisis of Trust
items.summary: Mormon Discussion host Bill Reel talks with historian Dr. Gregory Prince about his Dialogue essay “A Close-up View of Faith Crisis” and the decades of church decisions he says helped create Mormonism’s modern faith crisis.

items.title: The Deseret News Exposes Mormonism!
items.summary: A Generally Unquotable video responds to a Deseret News interview with author Melissa Dalton-Bradford on authoritarianism, comparing the characteristics she describes with Mormon church history, policies and leadership.
